questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The weather and the beach were crucial factors. Barcelona's warm, sunny climate and its beautiful coastline made it an ideal place for both academic pursuits and enjoying outdoor activities.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Very nice both academic and personal wise, but Barcelona is also a little bit dirty.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was not a problem at all; all the necessary information was provided via the email account set up by my new university.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There was an introductory day, but otherwise, you were mostly on your own. However, this wasn't an issue, as you could always contact an advisor if you needed assistance.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I used airbnb. It was very easy, and we had no problems, however, it wasnt the cheapest solution.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Some of my classmates experienced issues with bedbugs, so I would recommend choosing an Airbnb host that is a professional company rather than a private individual.

Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: it was a bit confusing, because it was a "bidding system", but ended up okay. Read next answer in relation to this:

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You had to bid on the courses you wanted to take, which was actually quite simple. The only issue was that you had to manually check that the courses didn't overlap, which took a bit of time.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Succesfull, i got all the classes i asked for, and there was no need for change.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Contract techniques and diplomatic law were very easy to pass.
Comparative law were quite interesting.
And negotiations skills were fun and interactive, but the one with the most preporation.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It wasn't very difficult; the teachers were kind, and it was nice not having too much homework and a short exam period. However, there is an 80% attendance requirement, so you need to be prepared to attend classes regularly, much like in high school.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The difficulty level is relatively easy compared to Denmark, so there's no need to worry. However, you do need to attend 80% of the classes. As long as you meet the attendance requirement and stay active in class, you're likely to achieve a good grade.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Very different from course to course. Some very interactive, some not. So you get a good mix.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
- Comparative law
- Negotiation skills
- Global sales law
- Contract techniques
- Refugee rights
-Diplomatic law

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Contract techniques and diplomatic law were very easy to pass.
Comparative law was quite interesting.
And negotiations skills were fun and interactive, but the one with the most preporation.

questions.answer: Different things. Football, mental health things and so on. I didn't participate though.

questions.answer: Don't know them.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I lived in el born. there you will find lots of nice restaurants. Otherwise hiking in the mountains close by. Also go see sitges, very nice city.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy. Reminded a lot of DK in many senses.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I didn't really meet any locals students no.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The language.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The food and nightlife.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Ik stress over skolen, blot mød op til timerne og sig noget.
Tag til Sitges eller marrakech.
Nyd vejret og havet i starten, det bliver sgu rimelig hurtigt koldere end man forventer.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Find et sted af bo i så god tid som muligt. Dem der gjorde det, fik de fedeste lejligheder til de bedste penge.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Jeg tror næsten jeg må sige bylivet faktisk. Det er ret vildt, hvor langt ud på natten og hvor mange mennesker der er. Men også den gode mad. Man bliver dog lidt træt af tapas, Kan anbefale luigis, rigtig god italiensk mad på via laitana.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Finde legater. Jeg modtog ikke nogle. Så start i god tid med det også. Det tager tid, men hvis man er dygtig vil det være tiden værd.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
